correctness.rationale: For n=7m+d and j=7k+e, Lucas factors the low digits. A carry from d+e>=7 makes the units digit of n+j smaller than e, so these terms vanish. This is also precisely where the corresponding low-digit binomial for A(d) vanishes; the surviving sum separates. Original-binomial evaluation at d=0,...,6 gives residues (1,5,3,3,3,5,1), and hence nonvanishing signs and digit sum -3. Splitting the cyclic correlation into low-digit carry classes proves the stated recurrence with the top-block wrap. The no-carry and carry signed sums give the displayed rows. With L=7^(r-1) and c=C_(r-1)(1)=(L+2)/3, the only boundary minimum is c-2L at h=5 and its negative; the boundary maximum is 2L+c<3L for L>=7. Interior cases have absolute value at most 9L/7, below (5L-2)/3. Multiples of seven inherit the sharp maximum and miss the new minimum by at least 4, including the step from r=1. The sign-pair count is obtained by expanding (1+sigma*s(n))(1+tau*s(n+h))/4 and using equality of the two cyclic marginals. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py 5` computes original binomial sums through n=342 and checks every correlation and sign-pair count at depths 1–3 (399 depth/lag pairs); the supplied CHECK.py was inspected, not executed. The proof, not the bounded checks, covers all depths.

value.rationale: A natural sign sequence from an established nonvanishing Apéry congruence has a precise scale-dependent distinction: the positive maximizer moves with the block depth while the most negative shift stays fixed up to sign. The exact finite extrema and their full equality sets quantify this difference; complete pair frequencies follow without assuming an unwrapped limit. This is not just a new tabulation of digit residues.
